assemble.prompt: Match each term to its definition.

items.label: Therapeutic cloning
items.clue: A process in which an embryo is produced with the same genes as the patient.

items.label: Embryonic stem cells
items.clue: Taken at the earliest stage of human development; can become most types of human cell.

items.label: Bone marrow
items.clue: Adult tissue containing unspecialised cells that can form many types of cell, including blood cells.

items.label: Meristem
items.clue: Plant tissue, found at the tips of roots and shoots, that can differentiate into any type of plant cell.

questions.stem: Which statement describes a stem cell?

options.text: A specialised cell that carries out one particular function.
A bone marrow cell that forms most cell types in the body.
An undifferentiated cell that can give rise to other cells.
A plant cell taken from the meristem tissue of a plant.

questions.explanation: A stem cell is an undifferentiated cell of an organism which is capable of giving rise to many more cells of the same type, and from which certain other cells can arise from differentiation.

questions.stem: Which statement about the function of stem cells is correct?

options.text: Meristem tissue can differentiate into any type of plant cell.
Bone marrow stem cells can differentiate into any type of cell.
Embryonic stem cells are specialised for one particular job.
Meristem tissue stops making new cells as the plant matures.

questions.explanation: Meristem tissue in plants can differentiate into any type of plant cell, throughout the life of the plant.

questions.stem: Which statement about therapeutic cloning is correct?

options.text: The stem cells produced are rejected by the patient's body.
The stem cells are taken from the patient's bone marrow.
An embryo with the same genes as the patient is produced.
The cells produced are specialised for one particular job.

questions.explanation: In therapeutic cloning an embryo is produced with the same genes as the patient, and stem cells from the embryo are not rejected by the patient's body so they may be used for medical treatment.

questions.stem: Which statement about treatment with stem cells is correct?

options.text: It is a guaranteed cure for conditions such as paralysis.
It uses bone marrow stem cells to replace nerve cells.
It fails because the patient's body rejects the cells.
It may be able to help conditions such as paralysis.

questions.explanation: Treatment with stem cells may be able to help conditions such as diabetes and paralysis.

questions.stem: Which statement about the risks of using stem cells is correct?

options.text: Viral infection could be transferred to the patient.
The concerns are ethical rather than medical ones.
Cells from a cloned embryo are rejected by the body.
The cells cannot give rise to more cells of one type.

questions.explanation: The use of stem cells has potential risks such as transfer of viral infection, and some people have ethical or religious objections.

questions.stem: Why are stem cells from meristems used to clone rare plant species?

options.text: Different plants are produced quickly and economically.
Identical plants are produced quickly and economically.
Identical plants are produced slowly and at a high cost.
Identical plants are produced while the parent is young.

questions.explanation: Stem cells from meristems in plants can be used to produce clones of plants quickly and economically, so rare species can be cloned to protect them from extinction.
